services of the company on 31.08.2002 rightly. As per the record and the mother record i.e. Old Form 
‘B’ it is evident that the deceased workman was rightly superannuated on attaining 60 years of age w.e.f. 
31.08.2002 as per the provisions of NCWA. He has also submitted Exhibit M-1 which is copy of 
Original Form ‘B’ Register. In Cross-examination he has admitted that the workman was appointed 
initially in BCCL on 10.08.1970. He can not say when Joyrampur Colliery was taken over by Coal 
Mines Authority. Form ‘B’ Register is prepared as per Mines Act. From their Office, information is sent 
to CMPF Office and it is a fact that in the service excerpts, the date of birth is 31.07.1955 and Exhibit 
W-4 Series are correct. He has denied the suggestion that he was deposing falsely. 


16. As regards the documentary evidence from the side of the management, Exhibit M-1 is photo 
copy of Form ‘B’ Register of Employees of Joyrampur Mines of BCCL and on its perusal it transpires 
that the name of the workman Samsul Mian has been mentioned on Serial No. 69 and in the column of 
age, 28 years has been mentioned and the column of signature/thumb impression, also bears the thumb 
impression but beside it the name of the person who put his thumb impression has not been mentioned. 
Exhibit M-2 is the copy of notice of retirement dated 04.05.2002 issued by the BCCL to the workman 
Samsul Mian informing that as he will attain the age of 60 years as per company’s record on 10.08.2002, 
he was informed that he was to retire from company service w.e.f. 31.08.2002 and he was also advised 
to avail the balance of earned leave/privilege leave before the expiry of retirement to collect the legal 
dues if any including gratuity etc. 


17. It is a fact that prior to the nationalization of coal mines as well as prior to the taken over of 
Joyrampur Colliery by the BCCL it was known as the Khas Joyrampur Colliery and after it was taken 
over by the BCCL in 1971-72 it was known as Joyrampur Mines under Lodna Area of BCCL. 


18. This is admitted fact that the concerned workman namely Samsul Mian joined Khas Joyrampur 
Colliery on 10.08.1970 i.e. prior to its being taken over by the BCCL after the nationalization and 
accordingly Form ‘B’ Register was prepared and declaration of Khas Joyrampur Colliery was separately 
prepared (Exhibit W-4 Series) in which the date of birth of the workman Samsul Mian was initially 
recorded as 31.07.1955. It is also evident from Exhibit W-4 Series that after it was taken over by the 
BCCL, the Identity Card of SamsulMian was issued by Joyrampur Colliery of BCCL on 20.06.1975 in 
which also his date of birth is very clearly recorded as 31.07.1955 (Exhibit W-5). Not only this, Exhibit 
W-6 was also prepared and issued by the Officials of BCCL which is Family Identity Card of the 
workman Samsul Mian in which also his date of birth is recorded as 31.07.1955 and in the year 1987 the 
BCCL itself prepared the service excerpts of workman Samsul Mian in which also his date of birth has 
been recorded as 31.07.1955 and it also bears signature of the BCCL Officers and therefore there is no 
reason to dispute the genuineness of these documents and MW-1 has also admitted in his cross- 
examination that Exhibit W-4 Series are correct. 


19. Now this is very surprising that Exhibit W-7 which is letter written by Dy. Chief Personnel 
Manager, Lodna Area to the Treasurer of the Union dated 06.04.2007 that as per new Form ‘B’ prepared 
in 1998, by mistake the date of birth of the workman is mentioned as 31.07.1955 which is clerical 
mistake and as such it was not taken consequent of which is a clear cut white lie and face saving stand of 
the management and so can not be accepted because Exhibit W-5 which is Identity Card of the 
workman Samsul Mian that was issued by the BCCL Officers about 23 years back on 20.06.1975 itself, 
his date of birth has been recorded as 31.07.1955 and in his service excerpts that was prepared in the 
year 1987 that also bears the signature of the BCCL Officers, the date of birth of the workman has been 
recorded as 31.07.1955 and therefore, on the basis of above discussion it is crystal clear that this is the 
management which is deliberately denying the date of birth of the workman Samsul Mian that was 
initially recorded as 31.07.1955 on the date of his initial joining i.e. on 10.08.1970 and it appears that 
subsequently the BCCL officials misplaced the entire original documentary records of the date of birth 
of the workman and so in the year 1998 it was deliberately distorted by the BCCL Officers and his new 
Form B was prepared and his age was then recorded as 28 years showing the same to have been 
recorded on his date of joining vide Ext.M-1 and so it can not be relied only on the ground that a thumb 
impression is there in the column of thumb impression without there being any name just below it 
showing whose thumb impression is this. So the stand taken by the management is quite baseless and the 
correct date of birth of the workman Samsul Mian was initially recorded in Original Form ‘B’ Register 
as well as several other documents (Ext. 4 series) as discussed above as 31.07.1955 and in such a 
circumstance the management can not be allowed to harvest the benefit of his own wrongdoings by 
forcibly retiring the workman Samsul Mian prematurely on 31.08.2002 instead of 31.08.2015 and most 


6602 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : JUNE 27, 2026/ ASHADHA 06, 1948 [PART II—SEc. 3(ii)] 


importantly all these documents on which basis the workman is claiming relief in this case, are not his 
private documents rather all have been issued from the offices of the BCCL itself and so it can not be 
allowed to disown it now and this is settled principle of law that if there are 2 types of different 
documents in BCCL relating to the date of birth of a workman, the document of date of birth favourable 
to the interest of the workman, must prevail. 


20. Thus on the basis of the above discussions of the facts, circumstances and materials available on 
the case record this Tribunal comes to the conclusion that the action of the management of Joyrampur 
Colliery under M/s. BCCL in superannuating Sri Samsul Mian, Pump Operator w.e.f. 31.08.2002 is 
neither legal nor justified and as per his correct date of birth as 31.07.1955 he must have been 
superannuated on 31.07.2015 and so he is entitled to the full back wages and all other consequential and 
retiral benefits for the rest of the periods upto 26.01.09 when he died. As the concerned workman has 
died, the management is directed to make payment of the above entire amount of arrears of money to the 
legal heir of the deceased workman within a period of 3 months from the date of the publication of this 
Award. The reference is answered accordingly.

In exercise of powers conferred under clause (d) of Sub-section (1) and Sub-section (2A) of 
Section 10 of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 (14 of 1947), the Government of India through the Ministry 
of Labour, vide its Order No. L-22012/136/2018-IR(CM-II) dated 22.11.2018 has been pleased to refer 
the following dispute between the employer, that is the Management of Poniati Workshop of Eastern 
Coalfields Limited and their workman for adjudication by this Tribunal. 


SCHEDULE 


“ Whether the action of the management of M/s. Eastern Coalfields Ltd. In relation to its 
Poniati Workshop in not rectifying the anomaly in basic pay of Sri Ram Surat Prasad compared to his 
junior Sri Shrawan Roy is just and legal? If not, to what relief the workman Sri Ram Surat Prasad is 
entitled to? ” 


1. On receiving Order No. L-22012/136/2018-IR(CM-ID dated 22.11.2018 from the Government of 
India, Ministry of Labour, New Delhi for adjudication of the dispute, a Reference case was registered on 
10.12.2018 and an order was passed for issuing notice to the parties through registered post, directing them 
to appear and submit their written statements along with relevant documents in support of their claims. 


2. Colliery Mazdoor Union, representing Ramsurat Prasad filed written statement on 04.03.2019. The 
fact of the case as disclosed in the written statement in brief, is that Ramsurat Prasad, Security Guard was 
promoted to the post of Head Security Guard at Poniati Workshop of Eastern Coalfields Limited 
(hereinafter referred to as ECL) in Technical & Supervisory Grade ‘E’ (hereinafter referred to as T&S 
Grade ‘E’) w.e.f. September, 2012. He was senior to Shrawan Roy in the same cadre who was promoted to 
the post of Head Security Guard, Poniati Workshop, T&S Grade ‘E’ w.e.f. November, 2014. The main 
contention of the union is that Ramsurat Prasad after his promotion was getting lower pay than Shrawan 


[भाग 1--खण्ड 3(ii)] भारत का राजपत्र : जून 27, 2026/ आषाढ 6, 1948 6605 


Roy, who was a Junior Head Security Guard and was promoted at a later stage. The grievance of the 
workman is that he was receiving a higher pay than Shrawan Roy before his promotion but after promotion 
of Shrawan Roy, the aggrieved workman received a lower pay, giving rise to anomaly in payment of 
wages. Management of Poniati Workshop did not issue any order to resolve the anomaly in payment 
between a junior and senior staff member. Accordingly, union raised the Industrial Dispute to sort out the 
anomaly. 


3. After issuance of Notice management of ECL filed written statement after five (5) years, on 
08.12.2023. It is disclosed that Ramsurat Prasad was appointed on 30.03.1990 and Shrawan Roy was 
appointed on 13.08.1990. Both the workmen were promoted to the post of Armed Guard Grade ‘F’ w.e.f. 
02.07.2005. Ramsurat Prasad was thereafter promoted to the post of Head Security Guard T&S Grade ‘E’ 
w.e.f. 22.08.2012 whereas Shrawan Roy was promoted to the post of Head Security Guard, T&S Grade ‘E’ 
w.e.f. 12.11.2014. Up to the month of October, 2014 the Basic Pay of Ramsurat Prasad was Rs. 29,142.47/- 
and of Shrawan Roy was Rs. 28,583.16/-. However, from the month of November, 2014, after Shrawan 
Roy was promoted, he received three percent (3%) as promotional increment and his Basic pay was fixed 
at Rs. 29,440.65/- but at the relevant time Basic pay of Ramsurat Prasad remained same at Rs. 29,142.47/-. 
According to the management Ramsurat Prasad had the benefit of promotion w.e.f. 28.02.2012 whereas 
Shrawan Roy was granted promotion w.e.f. 12.11.2014. Shrawan Roy received a Service Linked 
Promotion (hereinafter referred to as SLP) in January, 2014, as he did not receive any promotion in 
eight years since his earlier promotion on 02.07.2005. Thereafter, on his usual promotion on 12.11.2014 
his Basic pay became higher than Basic pay of Ramsurat Prasad. It is contended that there is no anomaly 
in fixation of Pay of Ramsurat Prasad as per the provisions of Implementation Instruction No. 14 
(hereinafter referred to as I.I. No. 14) under National Coal Wage Agreement - IX (hereinafter referred to as 
NCWA-IX), which applied to the employees of the Coal India Limited at the relevant time. The 
management of ECL asserted that according to the provision of I.I. No. 14 the case will come under pay 
anomaly under the following situations : 


“ (1) When the senior employee promoted to a higher post before 1" July 2011 draws less pay in the 
revised pay than his/her junior who is promoted later to the higher post. 


(2) Senior employee in the same pay and covered by the same seniority list and same designation in a 
cadre and who has secured fixation at the same stage as his junior but due to different dates of increment 
the junior starts getting higher pay than his senior. The removal of such anomalies will be subject to the 
following conditions : 


(a) both the junior and senior employee should belong to the same cadre and the post /grade /category 
in which they have been promoted should be covered by the same seniority list and same cadre, 


(b) the pre-revised and revised pay of lower and higher post in which they are entitled to draw pay 
should be identical; 


(० the anomaly should be directly as a result of application of normal rules of fixation on such 
promotion in the revised pay and as a result of fixation of pay in the revised pay under NCWA-LX. The next 
date of increment of the senior employee will be the same as that of junior employee. 


If even, in the lower post, the junior employee was drawing more pay in the pre revised pay than 
the senior by virtue of any advance increment granted to him. these provisions shall not apply in such 
cases. 


It has to be ensured that for removal of anomalies, the basic conditions stipulated above are 
fulfilled before initiating any action. 


This will apply to cases arising on or after 1 July, 2011. ” 


According to the management the date of promotion of Ramsurat Prasad and Shrawan Roy were different 
and their fixation of Pay was secured at different stages. Therefore, Ramsurat Prasad would not come under 
the purview of Pay anomaly provided in I.I. No. 14 under NCWA-IX. It is urged that the Industrial Dispute 
has no merit and is liable to be dismissed. 


4. The short point for consideration is whether the action of the management in not rectifying the 
anomaly in Basic pay of Ramsurat Prasad and Shrawan Roy is justified and legal. If not, what relief the 
workman is entitled to.

5: Union examined Ramsurat Prasad has examined himself as Workman Witness No. 1. He filed an 
affidavit-in-chief disclosing that in November, 2014 his Basic pay was Rs. 29,142.47/- whereas the Basic 
pay of Shrawan Roy was 29,440.66/-. It is stated that he is senior to Shrawan Roy and they have been 
promoted to the same grade 1.e., T&S Grade ‘E’ in the post of Head Security Guard. It is claimed that the 
management of Poniati Workshop failed to resolve the anomaly by fixing the Basic pay of Ramsurat 
Prasad at Rs. 29,440.66/- from November, 2014. During his examination-in-chief workman witness 
deposed that he was promoted to the post of Head Security Guard / Havildar in September, 2012 and his 
junior Shrawan Roy, promoted to the post of Head Security Guard / Havildar in November, 2014. On 
promotion Ramsurat Prasad received an increment of three percent (3%) of his Basic pay and in January, 
2014 his Basic pay was fixed at Rs. 28,293/-. The Basic pay of Shrawan Roy in January, 2014 was Rs. 
27,750/-. Thereafter in November, 2014 the Basic pay of Ramsurat Prasad was raised to Rs. 29,147/- 
whereas the Basic of Shrawan Roy on promotion was fixed as Rs. 29,440.66/-. The workman did not 
produce any document in course of his evidence. 


6. During cross-examination witness deposed that Shrawan Roy received a higher Pay of Rs. 298/- 
per month in his Basic pay than him and both of them were promoted to the post of Head Security Guard. 


7. Management examined Mr. Pragyanand Pandey as Management Witness No. 1. He filed affidavit- 
in-chief and produced the following documents in support of their case : 


(i) Copy of the Service Book of Ramsurat Prasad is produced as Exhibit M-1.

(vi) Copy of the Note sheet in respect of SLP granted to Shrawan Roy dated 24.01.2014, as 
Exhibit M-6. 


(vii) Copy of the Office Order dated 01.12.2014, whereby Shrawan Roy was promoted as Head 
Security Guard w.e.f. 12.11.2014, as Exhibit M-7. 


(viii) Copy of Application dated 11.02.2015 submitted by Ramsurat Prasad, alleging that there was 
anomaly in his pay fixation, as Exhibit M-8. 


(ix) Copies of the Pay Slips of Ramsurat Prasad and Shrawan Roy for January 2014, July 2014 
and November, 2014 are produced as Exhibit M-9 collectively. 


(x) Copy of Note sheet initiated for anomaly in Basic pay of Ramsurat Prasad, Head Security 
Guard and for the purpose of removing the anomaly, the authority revised his Basic pay to 
Rs. 30,323.87/- fixing his next date of increment as July, 2016, is produced as Exhibit M-10. 


(xi) Copy of the Master Amendment Advice relating to the pay fixation of Ramsurat Prasad, as 
Exhibit M-11. 


(xii) Copy of Office Order dated 24.08.2016, regretting the claim for removal of anomaly in Basic 
pay of Ramsurat Prasad, arising out of pay fixation of Shrawan Roy, as Exhibit M-12. 


(xii) Copy of I.I. No. 14 under NCWA-IX, as Exhibit M-13. 


(xiv) Copy of a Calculation sheet prepared by the Assistant Manager (Personnel), Poniati 
Workshop and signed by the Deputy Manager (Finance), Poniati Workshop where Basic pays 
of the two employees are compared, is produced as Exhibit M-14. 


During his evidence the management witness stated that according to LI. No. 14 under NCWA-IX 
Ramsurat Prasad is not entitled to any benefit by removal of anomaly in pay as he did not belong to the 
same cadre as Shrawan Roy and the management by Office Order dated 24.08.2016 (Exhibit M-12) has 
regretted the claim for removal of anomaly. Copy of the Office Order was served upon the workman.

8. In course of cross-examination the management witness deposed that management initially 
approved the claim for removing anomaly and increased the Basic pay of Ramsurat Prasad to Rs. 
30,323.87/- per month from November, 2015 (Exhibit M-10). The witness admitted that there was no 
official communication of the decision to Ramsurat Prasad by any order or letter that his Basic pay was 
increased to Rs. 30,323.87/- per month from November, 2015 and the next date of his increment was July, 
2016. Witness denied the suggestion that Ramsurat Prasad is entitled to the Basic pay at par with Shrawan 
Roy. 


9. Mr. Chandi Banerjee, representing the workman argued that Ramsurat Prasad being a senior 
employee than Shrawan Roy and being in the same cadre of Head Security Guard, T&S Grade ‘E’ is 
entitled to a pay protection by granting him same Basic pay as Shrawan Roy. It is claimed that Ramsurat 
Prasad was granted a promotion to the post of Head Security Guard, T&S Grade ‘E’ w.e.f. 22.08.2012, 
whereas Shrawan Roy who was in the same cadre and have been promoted to the post of Head Security 
Guard in November, 2014 are covered by the same seniority list. It is claimed that the pre-revised and 
revised pay in the lower and higher post in which both were entitled to draw was also identical. Therefore, 
according to I.I. No. 14 under NCWA-IX the Basic pay of the senior employee should be protected by 
removing the anomaly and his Basic pay should be at par with the Basic pay of Shrawan Roy, who 
received a Basic pay of Rs.29,440.65/- in November, 2014. 


10. Mr. P. K. Das, learned advocate for the management of ECL in reply urged that Shrawan Roy did 
not get promotion according to the same seniority list. After eight years of service, he was granted the 
benefit of SLP in January, 2014 and thereafter he was promoted to the post of Head Security Guard in 
November, 2014 with a benefit if three percent (3%) promotional increment of his Basic pay. It is argued 
that the Basic pay of Shrawan Roy stood higher than the petitioner workman. It is argued that the Ramsurat 
Prasad is not entitled to any protection of pay and there is no merit in the Industrial Dispute. 


11. I have considered the rival arguments advanced on behalf of the union and management in the 
backdrop of the facts and circumstances of the case disclosed in their pleadings and evidence adduced by 
the parties. It is gathered from the written statement of the management that Ramsurat Prasad and Shrawan 
Roy were appointed in service on 30.03.1990 and 13.08.1990 respectively. Both were initially promoted to 
the post of Armed Guard, T&S Grade ‘F’ on 02.07.2005. It is an all-accepted fact that both the employees 
belong to the same cadre at the source. Ramsurat Prasad being a senior was promoted to the post of Head 
Security Guard, T&S Grade ‘E’ on 22.08.2012 where Shrawan Roy was promoted to the post of Head 
Security Guard on 12.11.2014. The trajectory of their career indicates that both the employees, senior and 
junior, belonged to the same cadre and the post, grade and category to which they have been promoted is 
covered by the same seniority list and same cadre. It further appears to me that the pre-revised and revised 
Pay of lower and higher post in which they are entitled to draw their Pay is also identical. The anomaly 
cropped up due to grant of SLP to Shrawan Roy in January, 2014 and then a promotion in November, 
2014. Under such circumstances I am of the considered view that the Senior employee in the same 
seniority list who is receiving Basic pay less than the Junior employee, Shrawan Roy should be stepped up 
to the level of pay to the junior employee from the date on which the anomaly has arisen i.e., from 
November, 2014. Therefore, Ramsurat Prasad should get a Basic pay of Rs.29,440.65/- from the month of 
November, 2014 in place of Rs. 29,142.47/-. According to the provision of II. No. 14 under NCWA-IX, 
the anomaly which has arisen due to fixation of higher pay to the junior employee, Shrawan Roy on 
account of granting SLP in January, 2014 and thereafter normal promotion in November, 2014 has to be 
removed by stepping up the Basic pay of the senior employee equal to the higher Pay received by the 
junior employee. The next date of increment of senior employee shall have to be the same as the junior. In 
this matter the management has produced a Note sheet (Exhibit M-10) whereby it proposed to remove the 
anomaly in the Basic pay of Ramsurat Prasad by stepping up the same at par with the Basic pay of Shrawan 
Roy w.e.f. July, 2014 at Rs.29,440.66/-. Management in their Note sheet dated 03.12.2015 observed that 
the Basic pay of both the employees would be Rs. 30,323.88/- in November, 2015 and their next date of 
increment would be November, 2016. The management in this regard had issued a Master Amendment 
Advice dated 07.12.2015 (Exhibit M-11) where the Basic pay of Ramsurat Prasad was stepped up to 
Rs. 30,323.87/-. On a conspectus of the above facts, I find and hold that Ramsurat Prasad being a senior 
employee in the same cadre as Shrawan Roy and promoted earlier to the post of Head Security Guard in 
T&S Grade ‘E’ is entitled to an equal Basic pay as Shrawan Roy of the same cadre who was promoted to 
the same post at a later point of time 1.e., on 12.11.2014. It would be unconscionable if the anomaly in pay 
of the senior employee, receiving less than a junior employee in the same post / category is not removed. It

is therefore appropriate, just and proper and in accordance with LI. No. 14 under NCWA-IX, that Basic pay 
of Ramsurat Prasad should be stepped up at par with Basic pay of Shrawan Roy w.e.f. November, 2014. 
The management of ECL shall pay the difference of Basic pay and other consequential benefits linked with 
such Pay to Ramsurat Prasad, U.M. No. 268338 within two (2) months from the date of communication of 
the Award. 


Hence, 
ORDERED 


that the Industrial Dispute is allowed on contest against the management of Poniati Workshop of 
Eastern Coalfields Limited. Ramsurat Prasad is entitled to get the benefit of difference of Basic pay, at par 
with the Basic pay of Shrawan Roy from November, 2014 along with other consequential benefits. Their 
next date of increment shall be November, 2015. Management of Eastern Coalfields Limited is directed to 
pay the difference of Basic pay and other consequential benefits linked with such Pay to Ramsurat Prasad, 
U.M. No. 268338 within two (2) months from the date of communication of the Award. Let an award be 
drawn up in light of my above findings. Let copies of the Award in duplicate be sent to the Ministry of

AWARD 


In exercise of powers conferred under clause (d) of Sub-section (1) and Sub-section (2A) of 
Section 10 of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 (14 of 1947), the Government of India through the Ministry 
of Labour, vide its Order No. L-22012/6/2021-IR(CM-ID dated 19.04.2021 has been pleased to refer the 
following dispute between the employer, that is the Management of Bansra Colliery under Kunustoria Area 
of Eastern Coalfields Limited and their workman for adjudication by this Tribunal. 


SCHEDULE 


“ Whether the action of the Management of M/s. Eastern Coalfields Ltd. in relation to its 
Bansra Colliery under Kunustoria Area in denying the employment to the dependent son of Lt. Pathali 
Dhangar, Ex CC Maker, Bansra Colliery, i.e. Shri Rabi Dhangar is just and legal? If not, to what relief 
Shri Rabi Dhangar is entitled to? ” 


1. On receiving Order No. 1.-22012/6/2021-1२(( -11) dated 19.04.2021 from the Government of 
India, Ministry of Labour, New Delhi for adjudication of the dispute, a Reference case was registered on 
17.06.2021 and an order was passed for issuing notice to the parties through registered post, directing them 
to appear and submit their written statements along with relevant documents in support of their claims. 


2. Rabi Dhangar, dependent son of Pathali Dhangar filed written statement on 01.02.2023 through the 
President of Koyala Mazdoor Congress. Fact of the case as disclosed in the written statement is that the 
Industrial Dispute raised by the union due to denial of employment to the dependent son of Late Pathali 
Dhangar, an employee of Bansra Colliery under Kunustoria Area or Eastern Coalfields Limited 
(hereinafter referred to as ECL) who died in harness on 18.08.2013. The conciliation proceeding was held 
before the Assistant Labour Commissioner (C), Asansol for resolving the Industrial Dispute but the same 
resulted in a failure and the Government of India through the Ministry of Labour and Employment referred 
the Industrial Dispute to this Tribunal for adjudication. According to Rabi Dhangar he applied before the 
management for providing employment to him against the death of his mother. Supplementary documents 
were also filed, along with no objection from other family members and Indemnity bond signed by two 
permanent employees of the company. The management sought for certain clarification and production of 
documents from Rabi Dhangar. After more than two (2) years from the death of her mother, screening was 
held at the Colliery Level and the proposal for employment was sent to the Area Office. The management 
of ECL held medical examination of the dependent son where the Initial Medical Examination Board found 
him physically fit for his employment but observed that the age of Rabi Dhangar was between thirty-four 
(34) years and thirty-nine (39) years on 08.06.2016, i.e., on the date of holding medical examination. The

11. Having considered the arguments advanced on behalf of the union and management, on the 
backdrop of pleadings of the parties, facts and circumstances of the case and evidence adduced in the case, 
I find that Pathali Dhangar was a permanent employee of ECL and died in harness on 18.08.2013. A copy 
of her Death Registration Certificate is produced by the union as Exhibit W-2 which supports the fact that 
Pathali Dhangar died on 18.08.2013. The death information was communicated to the Manager 
(Personnel), Bansra Colliery by none other than Rabi Dhangar, the eldest son of Pathali Dhangar though 
his application dated 23.09.2013. Management has received the letter affixing a seal of receipt. The 
document has been admitted in evidence as Exhibit W-3. At the time of admission of documents 
management did not raise any objection on the ground of its genuineness. During cross-examination of

workman witness no suggestion was put to the workman witness, claiming employment that no such 
application dated 23.09.2013 and 18.12.2013 (Exhibit W-3 and W-4 respectively) were submitted by him 
claiming employment against the death of his mother. It is true that accompanying documents like 
Relationship Certificate and No Objection Certificate from other legal heirs of the deceased employee and 
Indemnity Bond were not enclosed with the initial application, claiming employment. Application 
enclosing death registration certificate and other documents like affidavit, attestation form, no objection 
certificate, photo identity cards were submitted for the first time on 10.06.2015 (Exhibit W-5 / M-1). On 
05.08.2015 the Agent, Bansra Colliery issued letter No. ECL/P/Per/15-16/1023 to Rabi Dhangar which has 
been produced as Exhibit M-7. On a perusal of the letter, it appears that management pointed out certain 
irregularities in the application of Rabi Dhangar dated 10.06.2015 and sought for clarification and 
production of few more documents. It is obvious that during consideration of a case for employment, the 
management may seek various clarification and compliance by production of additional documents. 
However, the initial application which has set the process in motion has to be considered as the date of 
submitting application for employment and not the latter application. The management cannot be allowed 
to take the liberty of considering the last application of the claimant as his application for employment, 
only to debar him on the point of his age. The management did not exhibit any promptitude on its part by 
responding to the applications of Rabi Dhangar dated 23.09.2013 or 18.12.2013 where he claimed 
employment soon after the death of his mother. It is only after spending two (2) years, management asked 
for some clarification through letter dated 30.07.2015 / 05.08.2015 (Exhibit M-7). Therefore, management 
cannot be allowed to take advantage of their own negligence. The IME Report (Exhibit W-9 / M-3) reveals 
that the age of claimant was assessed only on the basis of his appearance and no scientific examination was 
held. Be that at as it may, the age of the person concerned was assessed between thirty-four (34) years and 
thirty-nine (39) years on the date of the examination on 08.06.2016. Considering the midpoint of his 
approximate age it was found that he was thirty-six (36) years and six (6) months old on the date of 
medical examination. Rabi Dhangar was found medically fit for duty but the IME Board found him over- 
age on the date of his medical examination. In order to consider the eligibility of the claimant for 
employment, Coal India Limited has decided to reckon the age of the claimant on the date of submitting his 
application for employment. In the instant case, the applications for employment were submitted well 
within the time after death of Pathali Dhangar. The first application was submitted on 23.09.2013 and the 
second application was submitted on 18.12.2013. Management of ECL had remained silent about these 
applications and did not controvert such applications in course of cross-examination. It appears to me that 
at the time of submitting the application on 23.09.2013, the age of Rabi Dhangar was thirty-three (33) 
years nine (9) months fifteen (15) days, as per the assessment made by the IME Board. Clause 9.3.4 of 
NCWA provides that the dependents to be considered for employment should be physically fit and suitable 
for employment and their aged not more than thirty-five (35) years provided that the age limit in case of 
employment of female spouse would be forty-five (45) years. In so far as male spouse is concerned, there 
would be no age limit for providing employment. There is no reference in the NCWA regarding the date of 
reckoning the age of dependent for considering him for employment but in the letter issued by the Director 
(P&IR) of Coal India Limited bearing No. CIL:C-5B:JBCCI/943/163 dated 25.07.2003, it has been 
provided that the age on the date of submitting application would be reckoned for offering employment on 
compassionate ground. I therefore, hold that the management of ECL should have considered that Rabi 
Dhangar was medically fit and he was below the age of thirty-five (35) years on the date of his submitting 
application dated 29.09.2013 for employment in place of his deceased mother. Therefore, I find and hold 
that the decision of management denying employment to Rabi Dhangar by issuing later dated 29.06.2016 / 
01.07.2016 (Exhibit M-4), stating that he was over-age i.e., above thirty-five (35) years of age on 
08.06.2016 and not eligible for employment as per NCWA is unjustified, arbitrary, illegal, violative of 
provisions of NCWA and is liable to be set aside. 


12. It is pertinent to mention herein that in the case of Sukumoni Hembram alias Sukumoni Mejhan 
Vs. Union of India and Others [MAT 27 of 2024], the Hon’ble Division Bench of the High Court at 
Calcutta observed : 


“ NCWA is a negotiated agreement that has been arrived at between the employer and the employees. It is 
a settlement under section 2 (p) of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 and has binding effect on the parties 
thereto under section 18 (3) of the Act of 1947. NCWA has made provisions for compassionate 
appointment for the dependents of the deceased employee.”

I therefore, hold that this is a fit case where the management should provide employment to Rabi Dhangar, 
dependent son of the deceased employee as per provision of NCWA following the terms of settlement. The 
Industrial Dispute is accordingly allowed in favour of the union.

In exercise of powers conferred under clause (d) of Sub-section (1) and Sub-section (2A) of

SCHEDULE 


“ Whether the action of the management of Narsamuda Project under Sodepur Area of ECL in not 
providing employment to Shri Tapan Bouri, dependent son of Late Sundari Bouri on the plea of below 15 
years of age at the time of death of Late Sundari Bouri as such not qualifying 9.5.0 of NCWA and 
debarring his claim on the said clause without subjecting him to IME Board as Sh. Tapan Bouri has not 
passed High School Certificate Examination, is legal and or justified? If not, to what relief Shri Tapan 
Bouri is entitled to? ” 


1. On receiving Order No. L-22012/5/2016-IR(CM-II) dated 10.03.2016 from the Government of 
India, Ministry of Labour, New Delhi for adjudication of the dispute, a Reference case was registered on 
23.03.2016 and an order was passed for issuing notice to the parties through registered post, directing them 
to appear and submit their written statements along with relevant documents in support of their claims. 


2. The President of Koyala Mazdoor Congress filed written statement on behalf of Tapan Bouri on 
01.06.2016. In brief, the fact of the case as disclosed in the written statement of the union is that Sundari 
Bouri, the mother of Tapan Bouri was employed as TR Kamin at Narsamuda Project under Sodepur Area 
of Eastern Coalfields Limited (hereinafter referred to as ECL) as a permanent employee. She died in 
harness on 21.01.1998. According to the provisions of the National Coal Wage Agreement (NCWA) 
applicable to the employee and her legal heirs, one dependent is entitled to get employment. Tapan Bouri, 
the dependent son applied before the management of ECL for providing employment to him in place of her 
deceased mother. At the time of death of Sundari Bouri, Tapan Bouri her son was below eighteen (18) 
years of age and the employment proposal was not processed. According to the union if a dependent of the 
deceased employee is fifteen (15) years of age or above on the date of death of employee then according to 
Clause 9.5.0 of NCWA-V, the name of the male dependent is required to be kept in the Live Roster and 
female dependent, if any, would be paid monetary compensation. In the instant case there was no female 
dependent of Sundari Bouri. Tapan Bouri was more than fifteen (15) years of age and he was required to be 
provided with employment on his attaining the age of eighteen (18) years but the management did not 
provide him with employment. Union contended that according to Implementation Instruction No. 76 
(hereinafter referred to as 1.1. No. 76), if the dependent is a matriculate, his date of birth recorded in the 
Admit Card would be taken as final, but if the dependent is not a matriculate, then he / she would be 
referred to the Initial Medical Examination Board (hereinafter referred to as IME Board) for determination 
of age. In this case, the management did not refer the dependent to the IME Board before regretting the 
proposal for employment and thereby violated the guidelines of the company. Further case of the union is 
that after the death of Sundari Bouri, Tapan Bouri requested the management on 09.03.1999 that he was 
below eighteen (18) years of age and should be provided employment on attaining eighteen (18) years and 
also prayed for legal dues of his mother. The management did not process the prayer for employment on 
the plea that the defendant had submitted a belated claim but when it was pointed out that the dependent 
submitted his claim for employment soon after the death of his mother but the employment proposal was 
not processed as he was below eighteen (18) years of age, the management of ECL held a screening of 
Tapan Bouri at Colliery level and the proposal was sent to Sodepur Area. The management of the Area 
examined the file and regretted the proposal without assessing the age of the dependent. Union asserted 
that the age of Tapan Bouri was recorded in the Service Record of his mother as four (4) years in 1987. As 
such, the claimant was fifteen (15) years of age on the date of death of his mother. Union urged that Tapan 
Bouri is entitled to get employment under provisions of Clause 9.4.0 and 9.5.0 of NCWA.

3: Management contested the case by filing their written statement on 25.01.2023 after six (6) years. 
The main objection of the management is that as per Service Record of Sundari Bouri the age of Tapan 
Bouri is four (4) years on 01.04.1987. In the School Leaving Certificate of Tapan Bouri issued from 
Jagatdihi F. P. School the date of birth was recorded as 29.04.1984. Accordingly, the dependent son was 
below fifteen (15) years of age at the time of death of his mother. The contention of the management is that 
as per Clause 9.5.0 of NCWA-V applicable to this case, the age of the dependent should be fifteen (15) 
years at the time of the death of the employee, but in the present case, since the age of the son was below 
fifteen (15) years, he is not entitled to employment. Further contention of the management is that the 
application for employment was received at the office of ECL on 10.09.2010, after lapse of twelve (12) 
years from the date of death of Sundari Bouri. Therefore, the claimant is not entitled to any employment 
and the Industrial Dispute is liable to be dismissed. 


4. The central point for determination in this case is whether the management of ECL in not

applicable in cases of employment to dependents, the dependent son should be fifteen (15) years and above 
on the date of death of employee. In the instant case Tapan Bouri's age was above fifteen (15) years but 
below eighteen (18) years on 21.01.1998 but management did not provide him with employment, nor did 
management refer him before the IME Board for assessment of his age according to I.I. No. 76 which 
requires assessment of age of claimant if he is a non-matriculate. 


10. Refuting the claim of union Mr. P. K. Goswami, learned advocate argued that the age of Tapan 
Bouri at the time of his mother’s death was below fifteen (15) years and he was not found suitable for 
employment as per Clause 9.5.0(iii) of NCWA-V, which was not applicable until 01.01.2000. It is further 
argued that according to the Service Record of Sundari Bouri the age of Tapan Bouri was four (4) years on 
01.04.1987 (Exhibit M-3) and his date of birth as per Admission Register of Jagatdihi F. P. School was 
29.04.1984 (Exhibit M-2). Learned advocate submitted that the document was produced by none other than 
Tapan Bouri and it bears his signature. The said document goes to establish that the year of birth of Tapan 
Bouri is not 1982 and is 1984 and accordingly he was below fifteen (15) years of age on the date of death 
of his mother. Therefore, he is not eligible to get employment on compassionate ground as per provisions 
of NCWA. Learned advocate submitted that the Industrial Dispute raised is devoid of merit and liable to be 
dismissed. 


11. I have considered the rival contentions on behalf of the union and management in the backdrop of 
fact and circumstances of the case disclosed in the pleadings of parties and evidence adduced. Admittedly, 
Tapan Bouri was a minor dependent son of Sundari Bouri who died in harness on 21.01.1998 while in 
service of ECL. Tapan Bouri submitted an application for employment under ECL on 09.03.1999 (Exhibit 
W-5) while he was a minor. The copy of the application was received by the management of ECL and no 
objection was raised by the management at the time of admission of the document in evidence. Similarly, 
management did not raise any objection against another application of Tapan Bouri dated 11.05.2002 
(Exhibit W-6) wherein Tapan Bouri claim for employment. In view of such documents on record, I hold 
that there is no substance in the argument of management that the claim for employment was made after 
twelve (12) years, in the year 2010. Furthermore, management witness failed to produce Tapan Bouri's 
application dated 10.09.2010. 


12. It is now apposite to consider that whether the dependent son was entitled to employment as per 
the provision of Clause 9.5.0 (iii) of NCWA-V, which was made applicable to the employer company on 
21.01.1998. It is undisputed that the provision of NCWA-VI became applicable to the employer and 
employees from 01.07.1996 to 30.06.2001. The provision of Clause 9.5.0 (iii) of NCWA-VI was however 
made applicable only from 01.01.2000. It is axiomatic that the provision of provision Clause 9.5.0 (1) of 
NCWA-V bound the employer and employees until 31.12.1999. It would therefore be obvious that as per 
the provision of Clause 9.5.0 (iii) of NCWA-V, the age of the male depended on the date of death of the 
employees should be fifteen (15) years or above for maintaining his name in the Live Roster for the 
purpose of providing employment on attending eighteen (18) years. In the instant case, the primary 
document available to us for considering the age of Tapan Bouri is the Service Register (Exhibit M-2) from 
where it can be found that on 01.04.1987 the age of Tapan Bouri was four (4) years. Accordingly, his age 
was 14 years 09 months and 20 days on the date of death of his mother i.e., 21.01.1998. The Birth 
Registration Certificate (Exhibit W-5) of Tapan Bouri bears his date of birth as 29.04.1982. The document 
has been issued on 26.07.2023, has been obtained long after Reference of the Industrial Dispute for 
adjudication. Since the Birth Registration Certificate is neither contemporaneous nor issued earlier to the 
death of his mother, I am unable to place reliance upon the date of birth recorded in Exhibit W-5. In the 
letter dated 04.03.1998 (Exhibit W-4) issued by Bhudeb Bouri, the maternal uncle of Tapan Bouri, the age 
of Tapan Bouri has been stated as fourteen (14) years. Therefore, it would emerge from their own 
document that the age of Tapan Bouri was below fifteen (15) years on the date of death of his mother. 


13. Mr. Rakesh Kumar, union representative contended that the management did not refer Tapan Bouri 
to a Medical Board in terms with I.I. No. 76 which lays down the procedure for determining the age of a 


[भाग ए---खण्ड 3(ii)] भारत का राजपत्र : जून 27, 2026/ आषाढ 6, 1948 6619 


person, claiming employment, if he is a non-matriculate. On perusal of the provision of LI. No. 76 of 
NCWA-III, I find that its subject relates to : 


“ Procedure for determination / verification of the age of the employees and for resolution of disputed 
cases of Service Records.” 


It is clear that 1.1. No. 76 is applicable to existing employees of the company whose age recorded in the 
Service Record has been disputed. Evidently, the provision does not apply to a person claiming 
employment. Therefore, I hold that the management of ECL is not bound to carry out the procedure laid 
down in the LI. No. 76 for the purpose of resolving age dispute in respect of the person claiming 
employment as a dependent. 


14. It is a well settled position of law that claim for compassionate employment cannot be fulfilled as a 
matter of right unless the terms of offering employment to the dependents of the deceased employees have 
been clearly laid down by a prior settlement. NCWA lays down the guiding principles creating such rights 
of the employees. It is a settlement under section 2(p) of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 which has a 
strict binding effect on the parties thereto under section 18(3) of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947. The 
terms of such provisions are required to be strictly complied for their application. It is true that in NCWA- 
VI, Clause 9.5.0 (iii) governing the terms of employment had relaxed the lower age of the dependent by 
three (3) years and thereby permitted male dependents aged twelve (12) years and above to be maintained 
in the Live Roster w.e.f. 01.01.2000 in place of lower age limit of fifteen (15) years which was followed in 
NCWA-V. Since the terms of eligibility has been laid down under settlement the Tribunal does not have 
the discretion to interpret the provisions dehors the terms of NCWA. I am therefore, constrained to hold 
that Tapan Bouri who was below the age of fifteen (15) years on the date of death of his mother is not 
eligible for his employment under the management of ECL in terms of the NCWA applicable at the 
relevant time. The management of ECL therefore committed no illegality by denying employment to Tapan 
Bouri, the dependent son of Late Sundari Bouri. The Industrial Dispute is therefore dismissed on contest. 


Hence, 
ORDERED 


that the Industrial Dispute is dismissed on contest. The management of Eastern Coalfields Limited 
has not committed any illegality in denying employment to Tapan Bouri, the dependent son of Late 
Sundari Bouri as per provisions of National Coal Wage Agreement - V. Let an award be drawn up in light 
of my above discussion. Let copies of the Award in duplicate be sent to the Ministry of Labour,

As per letter dated 21/09/2015 by the Government of India, Ministry of Labour, New Delhi, the reference 
has been made to this Tribunal under Section-10 of Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 (in short the 'Act') as per 
Notification No. L-12012/85/2015-IR(B-J) dt. 21/09/2015. The dispute under reference relates to: 


"Whether the action of the management of State Bank of India is terminating the services of Shri 
Ashok Kumar Kashyap S/o Shri Nanhoo Prasad workman with effect from 18.04.1982 and not 
considering his name for reemployment while reemploying others including the recruitment of 
fresh hands in just fair & legal? If not, to what relief the workman concerned is entitled to?" 


Claimant/workman Ashok Kumar Kashyap (hereinafter stated as the claimant) has filed the statement of 
claim with averments which may be concisely stated as hereunder: 


(1) The applicant was employed by the State Bank of India, Regional office, Kanpur in the year 
1980 in subordinate cadre. The service of the applicant was terminated on 18.04.1982 in violation 
of the provisions of Section 25G of Industrial Dispute Act, 1947. After termination of the service 
of the applicant new hands namely Shyam Lal, Sarvesh Kumar & others have been employed in 
place of the applicant in violation of Section 25 G & H of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947. 


(II) The action of the employer in terminating the service of the applicant is illegal and is unfair 
labour practice because the applicant was working on the permanent post, but after termination of 
the applicant new hands had been employed in violation of Section 25G and H of the Act. This is 
also against the principles of natural justice. 


(II) The employer has done this type of unfair labour practice and illegal work and exploitation 
i.e. engaging one workman and terminating his service after few days and then again engaging 
another person and again terminating his services is being done with hundreds of persons. The 
applicant along with number of such other victimised persons started agitation by staging Dharna, 
demonstrations etc. against the illegal, unfair and unjust action of the State Bank of India. 


(IV) Thereafter, due to protest of the workmen, the State Bank of India decided to hold 
tests/interview so that regular and permanent appointment may be given to workmen who have 
already worked in the Bank. 


(V) The action of the Bank in holding test/interview was illegal because under the provisions of the 
Industrial Disputes Act 1947 the applicant was a retrenched employee and he was to be given 
appointment in the Bank not on the basis of any test/interview. But directly by the Bank as 
provided under Section 25 H of the Industrial Disputes Act 1947. 


(VI) It is submitted that the intention of the Bank was not fair throughout and bank wanted to get 
rid, by deceiving the applicant and other workmen, as such instead of giving appointment to the 
applicant. The Bank kept the name of the applicant in the waiting list. The Bank for malafide 
reason and unfair labour practice did not inform anything to the applicant nor published the waiting 
list in the newspapers or otherwise. However from the enquiries it came to the knowledge of the 
applicant that I have passed in the interview and my name was within 20 of the waiting list for 
giving permanent appointment in the Bank. It is requested that the Hon'ble Tribunal be pleased to 
summon the waiting list of 1991 from the Bank so that real facts may be disclosed before the 
Tribunal and justice may be done in the matter. 


(VII) Out of aforesaid waiting list of 1991 all most all the candidates have been appointed by the 
Bank but the Bank has not given appointment to the applicant. This is clearly unfair labour practice 
and illegal action of the Bank and it is also against the principles of natural justice. 


6634 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : JUNE 27, 2026/ ASHADHA 06, 1948 [PART II—SEc. 3(ii)] 


(VII) After the termination of the applicant so many new hand have been appointed by the Bank. 
As such the action of the Bank is illegal and unjust and the applicant is entitled to be reinstated 
with continuity of service and full back wages. 


(IX) The name of the applicant was within 20 of the waiting list of 1991. The applicant has not 
been given appointment but all most all the persons from the said waiting list have been appointed. 
As such the action of the Bank is illegal and unjust and the applicant is entitled to be reinstated 
with continuity of service and full back wages. 


Respondent side has submitted the written statement with averments which may be summarized as stated 
below: 


(1) It is essential to mention that to abuse/misuse of the provisions of the I. D. Act 1947[14 of 
1947] instant industrial dispute has been raised by the applicant regarding his alleged 
termination from 18.04.82. On this alone ground case is liable to be dismissed at the very 
outset by the Hon'ble Tribunal. 


(1) The alleged disengagement being of 1982 & 33 years have passed since then the industrial 
dispute cannot be said to have survived & a stale alleged dispute cannot be allowed be 
raised now. 


(ता) 1185 specific to state that to create illegal pressure upon the bank's management, General 
Manager, Kanpur have knowingly been made party by the claimant in the present dispute 
whereas claimant never worked for a day in both offices. It is made clear that relationship 
of employer & employee does not exist between the rival parties. In the light of above 
given facts claim is legally not maintainable & is deserved to be rejected forthwith by the 
Hon'ble court. 


(IV) It is clearly submitted that present case is out of ambit of continuous service as defined in 
section 25B of the Act because applicant never pleaded before the A.L.C.(C) that he had 
worked for 240 days at Regional Office, Kanpur therefore provisions of section 25 F do 
not attract in the instant matter. 


(V) It is necessary to add that claimant was not engaged in the bank against any post. To enrich 
our contention it is narrated here that there is a prescribed procedure for appointment in the 
respondent bank, which is evident from fact that appointment letter was not filed by the 
applicant along with his claim statement before the Hon'ble Court. 


(VI) _ Inclaim statement is mere reiterations. It is clearly submitted that applicant is not entitled 
to get relief claimed from the Hon'ble court. In the light of afore-mentioned true facts 
claim has no force of law & on the face of given reply case may be turned down by the 
Hon'ble Tribunal. 


Main question in this reference is that Whether the action of the management of State Bank of India is 
terminating the services of Shri Ashok Kumar Kashyap S/o Shri Nanhoo Prasad workman with effect from 
18.04.1992 and not considering his name for reemployment while reemploying others including the 
recruitment of fresh hands in just fair & legal? If not, to what relief the workman concerned is entitled to? 


In our claim statement applicant is requested that applicant was employed of the said bank in Regional 
Office, Kanpur in subordinate cadre and the applicant was terminated on 18.04.1982 in violation of the 
provisions of Industrial Disputes Act, 1947. And further says when we protest then the State Bank of India 
decided to hold test interview so that regular and permanent appointment may be given to workmen who 
have already worked in the bank. 


In accordance to that bank in holding test/interview was illegal because under the provisions of the 
Industrial Disputes Act, 1947. The applicant was a retrenched employee and he was to be given 
appointment in the Bank not on the basis of any test/interview. 


[भाग 1--खण्ड 3(ii)] भारत का राजपत्र : जून 27, 2026/ आषाढ 6, 1948 6635 


Due to malafide reasons bank did not give permanent appointment to the applicant. It came to the 
knowledge of the applicant that he have passed the interview and his name within 20 of the waiting list for 
giving permanent appointment in the bank. In that list almost candidates have been appointed by the bank 
but the bank has not given appointment to the applicant and with other facts in last requested that in the 
interest of justice Hon’ble Tribunal be pleased to give the following relief read as under: 


1. Reinstate in service with continuity of services and given full back wages and other 
attending benefits. 


2. Any other suitable relief which the Hon’ble Tribunal may deem fit under the circumstances 
and suitable cost of the case may please also be awarded. 


In reply of above claim statement bank filed written statement and in his written statement preliminary 
objection is raised that applicant regarding his alleged termination from 18.04.1982, which is not tenable in 
the eyes of law because above referred date of termination has not found place in claim statement & 
rejoinder statement filed by the claimant before the conciliation officer. 


Further in para stated that to create a legal pressure upon the bank’s management have knowingly been 
made parties by the claimant in the present dispute whereas claimant never worked for a day in both 
offices. It is made clear that relationship of employer & employee does not exist between the rival parties. 


Further in para 6 stated that claimant was not engaged in the bank against any post and further stated 
interview letter was not placed along with claim statement by the claimant before conciliation officer to 
prove his case. 


After filing of above written statement, rejoinder is also filed by applicant which is read as under: 


1. The contents of Para No. 01 of the written statement of the employer are wrong, baseless 
and misconceived hence are not admitted. In reply it is submitted that the services of the 
applicant has been illegally and unjustly terminated by the employer. The termination of the 
applicant is retrenchment. The employer has appointed new hands but has not given chance to 
the applicant as required u/s 25 H of the Industrial Dispute Act, 1947. The labour laws are for 
the welfare and protection from the exploitation of poor workman i.e. poor section of the 
society. Therefore the law makers i.e. the parliament of the country keeping all this facts and 
circumstances in consideration and passed experience did not mention any time limit for the 
re-employment of retrench workmen's in section 25 H of the Industrial Dispute Act, 1947. In 
view of these submissions no one including all courts of the country cannot and should not 
impose any time limit for raising such disputes in the name of old cases or belated case. As 
such the objection is baseless and misconceived as well as against the spirit of law and is liable 
to be rejected. 


2. The contents of Para No. 02 of the written statement of the employer are wrong, baseless 
and misconceived hence are not admitted. In reply it is submitted that the Case is for illegal 
termination i.e. retrenchment and also for not considering for re-employment in future 
vacancies as provided u/s 25 H of the Industrial Dispute Act, 1947. The employer has been 
giving employment to others but has refused to give employment to the applicant. Therefore 
the section of stale dispute or belated dispute does not arise. These are imaginary objection of 
the exploiting employer while there is no such provision in the Industrial Dispute Act. 1947. 
As such the objection is liable to be rejected out rightly. 


3. The contents of Para No. 06 of the written statement of the employer are wrong, baseless 
and misconceived hence are not admitted. In reply it is submitted that the applicant was 
engaged a clear post. The opposite part Bank is a very big exploiter; the opposite party 
engaged the applicant and after termination engaged another person. Thus the Bank is unfair 
labour practice, malafide and exploitation of poor workers and action of the employer is to be 
condemned. 


4. In reply to the contents of para No.18 and 19 it is submitted that the Government has 
power to refer any matter of any Industrial Dispute at any time. If once a reference has not 


6636 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : JUNE 27, 2026/ ASHADHA 06, 1948 [PART II—SEc. 3(ii)] 


been issued by the Government even then the Government can issue references order at any 
time. There is no illegality in it. The Hon'ble court is requested grant the relief claimed. 


5. The applicant is entitled to the relief claimed and in the interest of justices the same be 
kindly granted. 


Opposite party file documents/evidence on date 27.11.2020 is read as under: 
1. Copy of settlement 17.11.1987. 
2. Copy of settlement 27.10.1988. 
3. Copy of settlement 07.01.1991. 
4. Copy of settlement 09.06.1995. 
5. Copy of application moved by claimant before A.L.C. (C). 


Main question in this reference that applicant is employee in said bank as stated by him. 


After perusal of order sheets it shows that so many dates has been fixed for the evidence of applicant but 
applicant not produce any documentary/ oral evidence and A.R. of workman is withdrawn own authority 
on 29.12.2025. 


So, this is clear there is no any documentary or oral evidence is filed by applicant to prove his case such as 
appointment letter, interview letter, waiting list etc. 


The burden of proof to establish the existence of an employer-employee relationship and the alleged 240 
days of continuous service lies squarely on the workman. 


Despite multiple opportunities and several dates fixed for evidence, the claimant failed to produce: 


(i) Any documentary evidence (Appointment letter, salary slips, attendance records, or the 
alleged 1991 waiting list). 


(ii) Any oral evidence to substantiate his claims of employment or the alleged unfair labour 
practice. 


In the absence of any evidence, the claimant has failed to discharge the primary onus of proof. The mere 
filing of a statement of claim does not constitute proof of the facts alleged therein. 


Since the claimant failed to prove that he was an "employee" of the respondent bank or that any 
termination took place as alleged, the question of illegal termination or right to re-employment does not 
arise. 


Accordingly, the reference is answered in the negative. The claimant is not entitled to any relief. A 'Nil' 
Award is hereby passed. 


Parties are left to bear their respective costs.

2. और जबकि, केंद्र सरकार ने यूजीसी अधिनियम, 4956 की धारा 3 के तहत प्रदत्त शक्तियों का प्रयोग करते हुए, यूजीसी की सलाह 
पर दिनांक 45.03.2000 की अधिसूचना संख्या 9-26/94-यू.3 के माध्यम से इलाहाबाद कृषि संस्थान (एएआई), इलाहाबाद, उत्तर प्रदेश को 
सम विश्वविद्यालय संस्थान घोषित किया am इसके अतिरिक्त, शिक्षा मंत्रालय ने संस्था के अनुरोध और यूजीसी की सलाह पर दिनांक 
22.09.2009 के पत्र संख्या 3-7/2008-4.3(T) के माध्यम से “इलाहाबाद कृषि संस्थान” का नाम बदलकर “Aa हिगिनबॉटम कृषि, प्रौद्योगिकी 
और विज्ञान संस्थान” कर दिया। 

3. और इसके अलावा जबकि, कुलसचिव, सैम हिगिनबॉटम कृषि, प्रौद्योगिकी और विज्ञान संस्थान ने वर्ष 2047 में शिक्षा मंत्रालय से 
सैम हिगिनबॉटम कृषि, प्रौद्योगिकी और विज्ञान संस्थान का सम विश्वविद्यालय संस्थान का दर्जा वापस लेने का अनुरोध किया था, जिसमें यह 
सूचित किया गया था कि उत्तर प्रदेश सरकार ने दिनांक 27.(2.20(6 के वर्ष 206 के उत्तर प्रदेश अधिनियम संख्या 35 के माध्यम से उक्त 
संस्थान को सैम हिगिनबॉटम कृषि, प्रौद्योगिकी और विज्ञान विश्वविद्यालय के नाम से राज्य निजी विश्वविद्यालय स्थापित किया है। 


4. और जबकि, तत्कालीन यूजीसी (सम विश्वविद्यालय संस्थान) विनियम, 2040 (वर्ष 206 में यथासंशोधित) के अनुसार संस्थान के 
अनुरोध पर मंत्रालय में विचार किया गया और यह पाया गया कि यूजीसी विनियमों के विपरीत सम-विश्वविद्यालय संस्थान को राज्य निजी 
विश्वविद्यालय में बदलने से पूर्व मंत्रालय से अनापत्ति प्रमाण पत्र प्राप्त नहीं किया गया। 

5. और जबकि, जब यह मामला मंत्रालय के विचाराधीन था, तब संस्थान ने यूजीसी अधिनियम, 7956 की धारा 2 (च) के तहत 
विश्वविद्यालय की सूची में इसका नाम शामिल करने का अनुरोध करते हुए माननीय इलाहाबाद SY न्यायालय के समक्ष वर्ष 2049 में एक रिट 
याचिका (सी) संख्या 6583 दायर की। माननीय उच्च न्यायालय ने दिनांक 28.40.2025 के अपने आदेश के माध्यम से निदेश दिया कि यूजीसी 
इस तरह के समावेशन पर विचार करेगा, बशर्ते कि भारत सरकार की ओर से कोई विपरीत पत्र व्यवहार न हो, और यह कि तदनुसार कोई कानूनी 
बाधा सूचित की जाए। 

6. और इसके अलावा जबकि, इस मामले को विधि कार्य विभाग को उनकी विधिक राय के लिए भेजा गया। विधि कार्य विभाग ने राय 
दी कि इस मामले में कानूनी स्थिति का समाधान हो गया है और यह मामला अब प्रशासनिक प्रकृति का है, ऐसी टिप्पणी करते हुए कि माननीय 
उच्च न्यायालय के निर्णय को अंतिम रूप दे दिया गया है और इसका कार्यान्वयन इस मंत्रालय के अधिकार क्षेत्र में आता है और इस स्तर पर किसी 
अतिरिक्त कानूनी राय की आवश्यकता नहीं है। 

7. अब इसलिए, केंद्र सरकार विश्वविद्यालय अनुदान आयोग अधिनियम, 956 की धारा 3 के अंतर्गत प्रदत्त शक्तियों का प्रयोग करते 
हुए और विश्वविद्यालय अनुदान आयोग की सलाह पर विचार करके, WaT उक्त संस्थान के अंतिम बैच में प्रवेशित विद्यार्थियों के उत्तीर्ण होने 
के साथ ही दिनांक 45-03-2000 की अपनी अधिसूचना संख्या 9-26/94-यू-3 को वापस लेती है जिसके माध्यम से सैम हिगिनबॉटम कृषि, 
प्रौद्योगिकी और विज्ञान संस्थान (पूर्व में इलाहाबाद कृषि संस्थान), प्रयागराज, उत्तर प्रदेश को सम विश्वविद्यालय संस्थान घोषित किया गया 
था। इसके अतिरिक्त, सैम हिगिनबॉटम कृषि, प्रौद्योगिकी और विज्ञान संस्थान के प्रमोटर की यह पूर्ण जिम्मेदारी होगी कि वे उनके द्वारा अंतिम 
बैच के नामांकित छात्रों के हितों की रक्षा करें; पहले से उत्तीर्ण छात्रों के रिकॉर्ड/सामग्री को संरक्षित करें; सैम हिगिनबॉटम कृषि, प्रौद्योगिकी और 
विज्ञान संस्थान से संबंधित आधिकारिक पत्राचार /शिकायतें प्राप्त करें।पावती दें और साथ ही संकाय कर्मचारियों और गैर-संकाय कर्मचारियों जो 
सैम हिगिनबॉटम कृषि, प्रौद्योगिकी और विज्ञान संस्थान से जुड़े थे, उनके हितों को सुरक्षित करें।

MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(DEPARTMENT OF HIGHER EDUCATION) 


New Delhi, the 6th June 2026 


No. 9-26/94-U.3(A)—Whereas, the Central Government is empowered under Section 3 of the University Grants 
Commission (UGC) Act, 956 to declare, on the advice of the UGC, an Institution of higher learning as an Institution deemed 
to be University. 


2. And whereas, in exercise of the powers conferred under section 3 of the UGC Act, 956, the Central Government, 
vide Notification No. 9-26/94-U.3 dated 5.03.2000, on the advice of UGC, had declared Allahabad Agricultural Institute 
(AAJ), Allahabad, Uttar Pradesh, as an Institution Deemed to be University. Further, the Ministry of Education, on the request 
of the Institution and on the advice of UGC, rechristened the name of “Allahabad Agricultural Institute” to “Sam Higginbottom 
Institute of Agriculture, Technology and Sciences”, vide communication No. 3-7/2008-U.3(A) dated 22.09.2009. 


3. And further whereas, the Registrar, Sam Higginbottom Institute of Agriculture, Technology and Sciences requested 
in the year 207 to the Ministry of Education for withdrawal of Institution deemed to be University status of Sam Higginbottom 
Institute of Agriculture, Technology and Sciences informing that the Government of Uttar Pradesh, vide U.P. Act No. 35 of 
206 dated 27.2.206, has established the said institution as a State Private University in the name of Sam Higginbottom 
University of Agriculture, Technology and Sciences. 


4. And whereas, the request of the Institution was considered in the Ministry as per the then UGC (Institutions Deemed 
to be Universities) Regulations, 200 (as amended in 206) and found that no objection certificate was not obtained from the 
Ministry before conversion of the Institution deemed to be University into State Private University in contrary to the UGC 
Regulations. 


5. And whereas, while the matter was under consideration of the Ministry, the institution filed a Writ Petition (C) 
No. 6583 of 20l9 before the Hon’ble High Court of Judicature at Allahabad praying for inclusion of its name in the list of 
University under Section 2(f) of the UGC Act, 956. The Hon’ble High Court, vide its order dated 28.0.2025, directed that 
UGC shall consider such inclusion, subject to there being no contrary communication from the Union of India, and that any 
legal impediment be communicated accordingly. 


6. And further whereas, the matter was referred to Department of Legal Affairs for their legal opinion. The Department 
of Legal Affairs opined that the legal position in the matter is settled and the issue is now administrative in nature, observing 
that the Hon’ble High Court’s judgment has attained finality and its implementation falls within the domain of this Ministry, 
with no further legal opinion required at this stage. 


7. Now, therefore, in exercise of the powers conferred under Section 3 of the UGC Act, 956, the Central Government, 
considering the advice of UGC, hereby withdraws its Notification 9-26/94-U.3 dated 5.03.2000 declaring Sam Higginbottom 
Institute of Agriculture, Technology and Sciences (formerly Allahabad Agricultural Institute), Prayagraj, Uttar Pradesh as an 
Institution deemed to be University with effect from passing out of the last batch of admitted students. Further, it would be 
sole responsibility of the promoter of Sam Higginbottom University of Agriculture, Technology and Sciences to safeguard the 
interest of the last batch of students enrolled by them; to preserve the records / materials of already passed out students; to 
receive / acknowledge the official communications/grievances related to Sam Higginbottom Institute of Agriculture, 
Technology and Sciences and also to secure the interest of faculty staff and non-faculty staff who are/were associated with Sam 
Higginbottom Institute of Agriculture, Technology and Sciences.
